international.headline: 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference held in Cape Town
facts: The 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference (CPC) was held in Cape Town, South Africa, from September 13–19, 2026.
It was jointly hosted by the Parliament of South Africa and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) South Africa Branch.
The annual conference is a forum for Commonwealth parliamentarians to discuss parliamentary democracy, legislative practice and inter-parliamentary cooperation.
India’s delegation was led by Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh and included members of both Houses of Parliament and Rajya Sabha Secretary-General P.C. Mody.
The CPA was established in 1911 and is headquartered in London; its stated objective is to strengthen parliamentary democracy and cooperation among Commonwealth legislatures.
The Commonwealth of Nations is headquartered in London; King Charles III is its Head.
international.summary: Parliamentarians from Commonwealth countries met in Cape Town for the 69th CPC, with India represented by a delegation led by Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh.
international.staticLink: The Commonwealth Parliamentary Association promotes cooperation among legislatures in the Commonwealth.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 69th CPC was hosted in Cape Town by South Africa’s Parliament and the CPA South Africa Branch.
international.mainsAngle: Consider the role of inter-parliamentary forums in sharing legislative practices and strengthening democratic institutions.

national.canonicalTopic: India approves electricity exports to Nepal through December 2026
national.headline: India approves scheduled electricity exports to Nepal through 2026-12-31
facts: The Union Ministry of Power approved electricity exports to the Nepal Electricity Authority for 18 hours a day from 2026-09-13 to 2026-12-31.
Up to 600 MW is to be supplied through the Muzaffarpur–Dhalkebar 400 kV double-circuit transmission line and up to 54 MW through the Tanakpur–Mahendranagar 132 kV single-circuit line.
Export volumes from January 2027 were to be reviewed in December 2026.
The notes state that floods damaged Nepal’s hydropower infrastructure and reduced generation, increasing its need for electricity imports.
national.summary: India approved time-limited electricity exports to Nepal through two cross-border transmission links, with volumes for January 2027 scheduled for review in December 2026.
national.staticLink: Muzaffarpur–Dhalkebar is identified as a major India–Nepal electricity link; hydropower is Nepal’s primary electricity source.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The approved supply is up to 600 MW via Muzaffarpur–Dhalkebar and up to 54 MW via Tanakpur–Mahendranagar.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how cross-border electricity trade can support regional energy security and resilience after damage to generation infrastructure.

sources.title: India Approves Electricity Exports to Nepal until December 31, 2026

national.notes:
# 1. Approval
- **What:** Electricity exports approved for the **Nepal Electricity Authority**
- **Approved by:** **Union Ministry of Power**
- **Status:** **Approved** for **18 hours a day**, from **13 September 2026** to **31 December 2026**

# 2. Transmission links
| Link | Capacity | Line details |
|---|---|---|
| **Muzaffarpur–Dhalkebar** | **Up to 600 MW** | **400 kV**, double-circuit |
| **Tanakpur–Mahendranagar** | **Up to 54 MW** | **132 kV**, single-circuit |
- **Review:** Export volumes from **January 2027** scheduled for review in **December 2026**
- **Static fact:** Hydropower is **Nepal’s primary electricity source** [GK]

# 3. Context
- **Reason:** Floods damaged **Nepal’s hydropower infrastructure**, reduced generation and increased its need for electricity imports
- ⚠ **Trap:** The approval is time-limited through **31 December 2026**; volumes from **January 2027** were scheduled for review, not confirmed as unchanged.
# 4. Also note
- The Union Ministry of Power approved electricity exports to the Nepal Electricity Authority for 18 hours a day from 2026-09-13 to 2026-12-31.
> Exam angle: Link the **Union Ministry of Power** approval to the two India–Nepal transmission routes, their capacities and voltage levels.

national.canonicalTopic: Jayanti Prasad additional charge as IBBI Chairperson
national.headline: Jayanti Prasad given additional charge as IBBI Chairperson
facts: IBBI Whole-Time Member Jayanti Prasad assumed additional charge as Chairperson on 13 September 2026, succeeding Ravi Mital.
The notes state that Prasad’s additional charge would continue until 20 November 2026.
The IBBI was established on 1 October 2016 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies and information utilities.
national.summary: Jayanti Prasad took temporary additional charge as IBBI Chairperson while continuing as a Whole-Time Member.
national.staticLink: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies and information utilities.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Prasad succeeded Ravi Mital in additional charge from 13 September until 20 November 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Explain the role of the IBBI in India’s insolvency-resolution framework and the importance of institutional regulation.

sources.title: Jayanti Prasad Given Additional Charge as IBBI Chairperson

national.notes:
# 1. Charge and succession
- **Who:** **Jayanti Prasad**, **IBBI Whole-Time Member**
- **Post:** Additional charge as **IBBI Chairperson**, assumed on **13 September 2026**
- **Predecessor:** **Ravi Mital**
- **Tenure:** Additional charge until **20 November 2026**
- **Status:** **Additional charge** while continuing as a **Whole-Time Member**

# 2. Institution
- **Organisation:** **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)**
- **Established:** **1 October 2016** under the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016**
- **Objective:** Regulation of **insolvency professionals**, **insolvency professional agencies** and **information utilities**

# 3. Exam distinction
- ⚠ **Trap:** **Additional charge** is not the same as a permanent appointment as Chairperson.
> Exam angle: Identify **Jayanti Prasad’s designation**, his predecessor and the duration of his additional charge.

national.headline: India defeats Sri Lanka to win Women’s Asia Cup
facts: The 10th Women’s Asia Cup was held in the UAE from 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-13 in T20 International format, with eight teams.
India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final at Dubai International Cricket Stadium to claim its eighth title.
India scored 183/5 and Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111; Shafali Verma scored 68, Smriti Mandhana 59, Shree Charani took four wickets and Deepti Sharma took three.
India remained unbeaten throughout the tournament.
national.summary: India won its eighth Women’s Asia Cup title after defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final.
national.staticLink: The Women’s Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council and has been held in ODI and T20I formats.
national.prelimsTakeaway: India’s eighth title came in the 10th edition of the tournament.
national.mainsAngle: The growth of women’s cricket and the significance of sustained international performance.
